profile.reading:
STACK Infrastructure's POR03D is one of six buildings on the POR03 campus, part of the company's three-campus Portland market in Hillsboro, Oregon. STACK, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, operates roughly 8.5 gigawatts of capacity built or under development across 24 global markets, and Hillsboro has become an established Pacific Northwest data center hub alongside operators including Google, Digital Realty, and Infomart, drawn by the region's hydroelectric-heavy power supply, favorable tax treatment, and trans-Pacific subsea cable connectivity. POR03 spans 55 acres and 200 megawatts of total critical capacity as a campus. POR03D is the largest of the four individually specified POR03 buildings at 25 megawatts across 220,000 square feet, slightly ahead of sibling buildings POR03A, POR03B, and POR03C, each at 24 megawatts. STACK markets the POR03 campus toward AI, machine-learning, and cloud workloads and cites a low-water-use design approach for the site. Tenant identities are not publicly disclosed, consistent with standard industry practice. No street address, year of completion, named power utility, or independent local news coverage specific to POR03D could be located this session. These gaps are recorded rather than filled with unverified detail.

STACK Infrastructure has stated a company-wide commitment to net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, organized under five stated sustainability focus areas: carbon, energy, water, waste and circularity, and land use and biodiversity, publishing annual impact reports on its progress against those goals. Oregon's broader data center corridor, of which Hillsboro is the center, has drawn additional operators including Digital Realty, Infomart, and Google over the past two decades, aided by the region's enterprise-zone property tax abatement programs and Bonneville Power Administration-linked access to comparatively low-cost hydroelectric power, context that applies to the surrounding market generally rather than to this specific building alone.

reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure POR03 in Hillsboro, Oregon has 200 MW of total critical capacity across a 55-acre campus with 6 buildings, but only 72 MW is operational today and 25 MW is available for near-term deployment.

At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the 97 MW of operational plus near-term capacity would support roughly 2,400 racks. Oregon has published capacity of 156.6 MW across 8 mapped facilities. POR03's operational and near-term capacity represents 62 percent of the state's total disclosed capacity. The state contains 133 mapped facilities in OpenStreetMap, but only these 8 have published capacity figures, so POR03 is one of very few Oregon sites with a disclosed spec.

The site publishes no power interconnection details, grid connection status, or compliance certifications. Whether the 97 MW of current and near-term capacity can actually be energized depends on grid headroom and power availability that are not documented here. The 96 MW of expansion capacity depends on permitting, construction, and grid allocation decisions that the published spec does not address.
